blocks.text: A NumPy array has two parts. One part is the block of memory that holds the numbers. The other part describes how to read that block: the shape and the steps. A **view** is a new description of the same memory. A **copy** is a new block of memory.
The rule of thumb: slices with a start, stop, and step make views. Index lists and masks make copies.
Writing into a view changes the original array. Writing into a copy does not. This is the usual source of surprising changes in ML code, for example when you "clean" a slice of a dataset in place.
A view stores a start position and a **stride**. The stride is how many bytes to jump to reach the next element. The slice `a[::2]` uses a stride of two elements. It owns no numbers of its own.
